root_cause.text: The PPPoE receive path relied on the generic PPP layer to process protocol fields without enforcing that PPPoE sessions use an uncompressed 2-byte PPP protocol header, so compressed PFC frames were accepted and their payload became byte-shifted and misaligned.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states that “the current PPPoE driver assumes an uncompressed (2-byte) protocol field” but “ppp_input() is not aware of the negotiation result, and still accepts PFC frames,” and the fix adds an explicit `if (ppp_skb_is_compressed_proto(skb)) goto drop;` check in `pppoe_rcv()` to reject compressed protocol frames.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the shared PPP compressed-protocol check when deciding whether to restore the leading protocol byte in received sk_buffs.
intent_record.what: The direct check `skb->data[0] & 0x01` in `__ppp_decompress_proto(struct sk_buff *skb)` was replaced with a call to `ppp_skb_is_compressed_proto(skb)` while keeping the same conditional body that prepends a zero byte to the skb data.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the decision of whether a PPP protocol field is compressed is now delegated to the helper function instead of being inferred from the first data byte inline, which centralizes the detection logic and can correct or standardize protocol-compression handling for sk_buffs before expanding the protocol field.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the PPPoE session header length constant when validating received skb data in pppoe_rcv().
intent_record.what: The call to pskb_may_pull() in pppoe_rcv() was changed to use PPPOE_SES_HLEN instead of sizeof(struct pppoe_hdr) as the required header length before accessing the PPPoE header.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the receive path now validates that the skb contains at least the full PPPoE session header length as defined by the protocol constant, preventing packets with insufficient pulled data from being processed under a potentially incorrect size assumption.

intent_record.intent_summary: Drop compressed-protocol PPPoE frames during receive handling to prevent unsupported PFC packets from being processed.
intent_record.what: A new check was added in pppoe_rcv() after the skb length validation and before pskb_trim_rcsum() to call ppp_skb_is_compressed_proto(skb), with an accompanying comment explaining that skb->data points to the PPP protocol header after skb_pull_rcsum; if the packet uses a compressed PPP protocol field, execution jumps to the drop path.
intent_record.how: At runtime, PPPoE receive processing now rejects and drops PFC (Protocol Field Compression) frames instead of continuing normal packet handling, preventing unsupported or invalid compressed-protocol PPP frames from being processed further.

intent_record.intent_summary: Include linux/skbuff.h in ppp_defs.h so sk_buff-related definitions are available and dependent PPP code builds correctly.
intent_record.what: A new header include, #include <linux/skbuff.h>, was added to ppp_defs.h alongside the existing includes for linux/crc-ccitt.h and uapi/linux/ppp_defs.h.
intent_record.how: This makes sk_buff-related type or macro declarations available wherever ppp_defs.h is included, preventing build issues caused by missing skbuff definitions and ensuring dependent code can compile correctly.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a helper to detect compressed PPP protocol fields directly from an sk_buff header.
intent_record.what: A new static inline helper function, ppp_skb_is_compressed_proto(const struct sk_buff *skb), was added to the PPP header file along with a kernel-doc comment block. The function reads skb->data[0] and returns unlikely(skb->data[0] & 0x01) to indicate whether the PPP protocol field is compressed.
intent_record.how: This change introduces a reusable runtime check for detecting a compressed PPP protocol field when skb->data points at the PPP protocol header. It enables callers to determine protocol compression directly from an sk_buff without duplicating the bit test logic, but does not itself alter behavior unless used elsewhere.

consistency_review.core_intent: Ensure PPPoE receive handling correctly identifies and rejects compressed-protocol (PFC) frames by using the shared PPP protocol-compression check.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly target the root cause by detecting PPP compressed-protocol (PFC) frames in the PPPoE receive path and rejecting them, enforcing the required uncompressed 2-byte PPP protocol header and preventing the byte-shifted/misaligned payload issue.

This change only switches validation to use the PPPoE session header length constant when checking received skb length. It does not enforce or reject compressed PPP protocol fields/PFC frames, which is the core cause of the misaligned payload vulnerability.

This change only adds a header include for sk_buff definitions to fix/build PPP-related code dependencies. It does not affect PPPoE receive-path validation, PPP protocol field parsing, or enforcement of the required uncompressed 2-byte PPP protocol header.

The root cause is acceptance of compressed PPP protocol fields in PPPoE sessions. Adding a helper to detect compressed PPP protocol fields directly from an sk_buff header is directly tied to identifying and handling/rejecting those invalid compressed frames, so it addresses the vulnerability mechanism.

candidates.rationale: The PPPoE receive path trimmed and accepted the frame based only on length, with no validation that the PPP protocol field was the required uncompressed 2-byte form. This allowed compressed PFC frames to continue into generic PPP processing and become misaligned.

This shows the receive path only enforced size bounds before processing, not the PPPoE-specific requirement to reject compressed protocol headers, contributing to acceptance of malformed PFC session frames.

Generic PPP logic inferred protocol compression from the first protocol byte and restored a missing leading zero. Relying on this behavior for PPPoE was unsafe because PPPoE sessions require an uncompressed 2-byte protocol field, so compressed frames should have been rejected earlier.

This statement actively reconstructs a compressed PPP protocol field by prepending a zero byte. In the PPPoE receive path this behavior is invalid, because PPPoE must not accept PFC-compressed frames; restoring them causes payload interpretation to proceed on unsupported input.

vuln_statements.explanation: This receive-path statement shows the PPPoE code accepted and normalized the packet based on length trimming alone, without validating that the PPP protocol field was the required uncompressed 2-byte form. That omission allowed compressed PFC frames to proceed into generic PPP handling, leading to the byte-shift/misalignment root cause.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function is sufficient because it contains the PPPoE receive-path logic that validates and forwards the received session payload. After pulling the PPPoE header (`skb_pull_rcsum(skb, sizeof(*ph));`), the code only checks the PPPoE payload length (`if (skb->len < len) goto drop;` and `if (pskb_trim_rcsum(skb, len)) goto drop;`) and then immediately looks up the socket and delivers the skb (`return sk_receive_skb(sk_pppox(po), skb, 0);`). There is no validation that the PPP payload begins with the required uncompressed 2-byte PPP protocol field for PPPoE sessions, and no rejection of PFC/compressed protocol frames. That matches the root cause: the PPPoE layer relies on generic PPP processing and accepts compressed frames, allowing the payload to be byte-shifted/misaligned. The commit message and code only address socket lookup/trim ordering, not PPP protocol-field enforcement, so the fix is not present.
